title: Popescu's theorem: regular maps of Noetherian rings are filtered colimits of smooth algebras
statement: Let $R$ and $\Lambda$ be Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $\varphi:R\to\Lambda$ a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] (flat, with Noetherian geometrically regular fibre rings $\Lambda\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$). Then $\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras: there are a small filtered category $J$ and a functor $j\mapsto B_j$ from $J$ to commutative $R$-algebras (with $R$-algebra transition maps) such that $\operatorname{Spec}B_j\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] for every $j$, and $R$-algebra maps $\iota_j:B_j\to\Lambda$ such that $(\Lambda,(\iota_j)_j)$ is a colimit of the diagram $j\mapsto B_j$ in the category of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Theorem Tag 07GC (theorem-popescu): 'Any regular homomorphism of Noetherian rings is a filtered colimit of smooth ring maps'; its proof occupies the whole chapter (Lemma lemma-reduce-to-field, Lemma lemma-final-solve, and the Noetherian induction on the ideal h_A). Smooth ring maps R -> B_j correspond to smooth morphisms Spec B_j -> Spec R (Morphisms, Definition 01V5 and Lemma 01V6, lemma-smooth-characterize)

proof.text: Reduction to a field. By [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-reduce-to-field] it suffices to show: for every field $k$ and every Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ with a regular ring map $k\to\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], $\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $k$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras]; this then holds for every regular map $R\to\Lambda$ of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (Step 6 translates the conclusion into the form of the statement). Fix such $k\to\Lambda$. The only prime of $k$ is $(0)$, with $k_{(0)}=k$ and $\kappa((0))=k$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], so the fibre ring of $\Lambda$ over $(0)$ is $\Lambda\otimes_kk\cong\Lambda$; by the definition of a regular ring map, $\Lambda$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. In particular $\Lambda$ is regular: $k/k$ is a finite purely inseparable extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] (of degree $1$; every $\alpha\in k$ has $\alpha^{p^0}\in k$ in characteristic $p$, and $k'=k$ in characteristic $0$), so $k\otimes_k\Lambda\cong\Lambda$ is regular, i.e. every $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Theorem Tag 07GC (theorem-popescu): 'By Lemma lemma-reduce-to-field (Tag 07F5) it suffices to prove this for k -> Lambda where Lambda is Noetherian and geometrically regular over k'

proof.text: Reduction to factorizations. Let $\mathcal E$ be the set of $k$-algebras of the form $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/I$ ($n\ge0$, $I$ an ideal) that are smooth over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]; they are of finite presentation by definition of smoothness. Every smooth $k$-algebra $B$ is finitely presented, hence isomorphic as a $k$-algebra to a member of $\mathcal E$. So by [lem-weil-pbc-factorization-criterion-filtered-colimit], $\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of members of $\mathcal E$, i.e. of smooth $k$-algebras in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras], as soon as: (*) for every $k$-algebra $A$ of finite presentation and every $k$-algebra homomorphism $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ there are a smooth $k$-algebra $D$ and $k$-algebra maps $A\to D\to\Lambda$ with composite $\alpha$ (replace $D$ by an isomorphic member of $\mathcal E$, composing the maps with the isomorphism). Steps 3-5 prove (*).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Theorem Tag 07GC (theorem-popescu): 'Let k -> A -> Lambda be a factorization with A a finite type k-algebra. It suffices to construct a factorization A -> B -> Lambda with B ...'; the criterion is Algebra, Lemma Tag 07C3 (lemma-when-colimit), as cited in the proof of Lemma 07F5

proof.text: Resolution at a minimal prime. Let $B$ be a $k$-algebra of finite presentation, $\gamma:B\to\Lambda$ a $k$-algebra map, $\mathfrak h_B=\sqrt{H_{B/k}\Lambda}$ [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution] (with the singular ideal $H_{B/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]), and $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ a prime minimal over $\mathfrak h_B$. Then $k\to B\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$ can be resolved [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution] ($k$ is a field, hence Noetherian). The characteristic of $k$ is $0$ or a prime $p$. If it is $0$: $\Lambda$ is Noetherian, $\mathfrak q$ is minimal over $\mathfrak h_B$, $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring by Step 1, and $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is separable over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] by [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-separable]; so [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-resolve-separable] applies. If it is $p>0$: $\Lambda$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $k$ by Step 1 and $\mathfrak q$ is minimal over $\mathfrak h_B$, so [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-resolve-char-p] applies.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Theorem Tag 07GC (theorem-popescu): 'It now suffices to resolve k -> A -> Lambda ⊃ q (as defined in the text following Situation 07F7). If the characteristic of k is zero, this follows from Lemma lemma-resolve-special (Tag 07FE). If the characteristic of k is p > 0, this follows from Lemma lemma-resolve-general (Tag 07FJ)'; that every field extension in characteristic zero is separable is used without proof in Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TX

proof.text:
Noetherian induction on $\mathfrak h$. Fix $A$ and $\alpha:A	o\Lambda$ as in (*). Let $\Phi$ be the set of ideals $\mathfrak h_B=\sqrt{H_{B/k}\Lambda}\subset\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution], for all factorizations $A	o B\xrightarrow{\gamma}\Lambda$ of $\alpha$ by $k$-algebra maps with $B$ of finite presentation over $k$; $\Phi
e\emptyset$ ($B=A$). As $\Lambda$ is Noetherian, $\Phi$ has a maximal element $\mathfrak h_B$ [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-ideal-set-maximal], for some such factorization $A	o B	o\Lambda$. Claim: $\mathfrak h_B=\Lambda$. Otherwise $\mathfrak h_B$ is a proper ideal and there is a prime $\mathfrak q\supset\mathfrak h_B$ minimal over $\mathfrak h_B$ [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-over-proper-ideal]. By Step 3 there is a resolution $B	o C	o\Lambda$ of $k	o B	o\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$: $C$ of finite presentation over $k$, $\mathfrak h_B\subset\mathfrak h_C$ and $\mathfrak h_C
ot\subset\mathfrak q$. Then $A	o B	o C	o\Lambda$ is a factorization of $\alpha$, so $\mathfrak h_C\in\Phi$, and $\mathfrak h_C
eq\mathfrak h_B$ because $\mathfrak h_B\subset\mathfrak q$; hence $\mathfrak h_B\subsetneq\mathfrak h_C$, contradicting maximality. So there is a factorization $A	o B	o\Lambda$ with $B$ of finite presentation over $k$ and $\mathfrak h_B=\Lambda$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Theorem Tag 07GC (theorem-popescu): 'Hence we may perform Noetherian induction on the ideal h_A. Pick a prime q ⊃ h_A such that q is minimal over h_A.'

proof.text: Final solve. With $A\to B\xrightarrow{\gamma}\Lambda$ from Step 4: $1\in\mathfrak h_B=\sqrt{H_{B/k}\Lambda}$ gives $1=1^n\in H_{B/k}\Lambda$, i.e. $H_{B/k}\Lambda=\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. By [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-final-solve] (applied to $k\to B\to\Lambda$, $B$ of finite presentation) there are a smooth $k$-algebra $D$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and $k$-algebra maps $B\to D\to\Lambda$ with composite $\gamma$. Then $A\to B\to D\to\Lambda$ has composite $\alpha$, which proves (*). By Step 2, $\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $k$-algebras, and by Step 1, for every regular ring map $R\to\Lambda$ of Noetherian rings, $\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Theorem Tag 07GC (theorem-popescu): 'It suffices to construct a factorization A -> B -> Lambda with B of finite type such that h_B = Lambda, see Lemma lemma-final-solve (Tag 07EU)'

proof.text: The form of the statement. Let $R\to\Lambda$ be regular with $R,\Lambda$ Noetherian. By Step 5 there are a small filtered category $J$, a functor $j\mapsto B_j$ to commutative $R$-algebras with every $B_j$ a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and $R$-algebra maps $\iota_j:B_j\to\Lambda$ forming a colimit in commutative $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras]. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], each $\operatorname{Spec}B_j\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (1), $(\Lambda,(\iota_j)_j)$ is also a colimit of the underlying diagram of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. This is the statement.
